title: AC1024 opaque callback source retention and strict output gate

source.fixturePolicy: Used the existing local sample matching the previously recorded source digest. No DWG/DXF fixture was added to Git.

behavior: Retain generic unsupported DWG callback bodies in a generation/handle keyed adapter store with 100,000-record and 64 MiB limits.
Count source retention separately from the legacy ACDS correlation counter and from output qualification.
Strict read completeness now requires every opaque callback view to have a retained source frame and rejects capture failure.
Strict export has a distinct output-admission gate; retained bytes alone do not qualify output.
limitations: The generic store retains callback bodies, not a complete physical DWG object-map frame or a DXF replay representation.
No opaque callback output proofs are currently recorded. Strict complete-export remains refused.

coverage: Exact callback-body copy, generation key, duplicate identity refusal, malformed-span refusal, sticky failure, corrected next-generation retry and byte-budget refusal.
Strict export refuses a complete retained source frame until separate per-identity output qualification exists; a count-only value does not pass the gate.
Existing ACDS and standard-object capture controls remain passing.

strictCheckpoint.result: REFUSED before publication at the distinct output gate; no DXF was created.
strictCheckpoint.diagnostic: strict-complete conversion requires output qualification for every opaque DWG callback

validation.fullSuites: NOT RUN; focused adapter cohort and one strict CLI checkpoint used.

planImpact.completedActionRemoved: Generic opaque callback source bodies are retained under bounds, and strict read retention is separated from strict output qualification.
planImpact.nextAction: Bind the highest-incidence remaining callback family to complete typed output or a proven end-to-end replay route, including owner/dependency closure and fresh readback; keep the strict gate closed until every required callback is qualified.
